description: Stance-gate label precision: 123 stage_3 representative_quotes from two runs (coffee roasters, live music venues) hand-labeled SUPPORTS/TOPICAL/OFFTOPIC/PROMO against each pain's own title+description; non-SUPPORTS quotes carry a one-line reason.

cases.pain_title: Cannot maintain café and subscription supply when spot coffee disappears
cases.pain_description: Café-based roasters and subscription businesses need dependable recurring supply, but spot coffee can become unavailable or expensive. This blocks reliable café roast schedules and recurring shipments when the same bean is no longer available.
cases.quote: Yeah I had spent a couple grand on green coffee from them over a couple years and went elsewhere after that debacle.
cases.label: TOPICAL
cases.reason: Supplier-relationship complaint, not a supply-continuity/substitution failure.

cases.pain_title: Cannot maintain café and subscription supply when spot coffee disappears
cases.pain_description: Café-based roasters and subscription businesses need dependable recurring supply, but spot coffee can become unavailable or expensive. This blocks reliable café roast schedules and recurring shipments when the same bean is no longer available.
cases.quote: But because of the poor state of the spot market it’s a bad time to try to find a coffee for the gap.
cases.label: SUPPORTS

cases.pain_title: Cannot reject defective green coffee reliably before committing to a lot
cases.pain_description: Green coffee buyers and quality-control staff struggle to identify whether bad beans, moldy sour insect damage, or defects present originated in the crop, transport, storage, or supplier selection. A lot may become unusable before roasting.
cases.quote: Will just touch on green freshness - temperature matters, how they’re stored matters, what happened before they arrived matters but fundamentally you don’t want to be in the habit of punting coffee which is over a year past harvest, sometimes you get lucky but mostly it’ll be past its best.
cases.label: TOPICAL
cases.reason: Generic freshness/storage advice, not about rejecting a defective lot before commit.

cases.pain_title: Cannot reject defective green coffee reliably before committing to a lot
cases.pain_description: Green coffee buyers and quality-control staff struggle to identify whether bad beans, moldy sour insect damage, or defects present originated in the crop, transport, storage, or supplier selection. A lot may become unusable before roasting.
cases.quote: In specialty we often have lot separation for different farms, processes or even pick dates.
cases.label: TOPICAL
cases.reason: Neutral explanation of lot-separation practice, not defect rejection.

cases.pain_title: Cannot verify storage and water activity before green coffee production
cases.pain_description: Roasters cannot consistently confirm that green coffee was stored properly or that an old crop retained stable moisture. GrainPro bag condition and water activity are difficult to connect to later roast performance.
cases.quote: Will just touch on green freshness - temperature matters, how they’re stored matters, what happened before they arrived matters but fundamentally you don’t want to be in the habit of punting coffee which is over a year past harvest, sometimes you get lucky but mostly it’ll be past its best.
cases.label: TOPICAL
cases.reason: Generic advice, not a person unable to verify storage/water activity.

cases.pain_title: Cannot verify storage and water activity before green coffee production
cases.pain_description: Roasters cannot consistently confirm that green coffee was stored properly or that an old crop retained stable moisture. GrainPro bag condition and water activity are difficult to connect to later roast performance.
cases.quote: Unfortunately the coffee supply chain is a bit of a mess right now so when really good coffees are available I suggest you get as much as you can use and store well for about a year, really good coffees last at least a year coffee that wasn't so good to begin with may have a sweet spot of a few months.
cases.label: TOPICAL
cases.reason: Advice on stockpiling/aging, not verification failure.

cases.pain_title: Cannot transfer roast curves from sample equipment to production machines
cases.pain_description: Roasters struggle to reproduce a target roast when moving from sample equipment to production equipment or between different machines. The same roast curves and drop temperatures do not reliably produce the same color or flavor.
cases.quote: But recording the roast profile and entering your fan, heat, and drum speed changes make it easy to manually duplicate that BT curve given the same environmental conditions, bean choice and amount, and electrical supply consistency.
cases.label: TOPICAL
cases.reason: States the problem IS solvable with recording discipline; solved-problem framing.

cases.pain_title: Cannot transfer roast curves from sample equipment to production machines
cases.pain_description: Roasters struggle to reproduce a target roast when moving from sample equipment to production equipment or between different machines. The same roast curves and drop temperatures do not reliably produce the same color or flavor.
cases.quote: Play with it and slowly learn the ropes but you cant replicate easily what Rogue Wave has been producing or other roasters out there like Parlor Coffee or Onyx Coffe Lab.
cases.label: TOPICAL
cases.reason: About matching other roasters' quality generally, not sample→production equipment transfer.

cases.pain_title: Cannot scale sample roast settings to café production volume
cases.pain_description: Café-based and wholesale roasters struggle to scale sample roast settings to larger production batches. Different batch sizes and drop temperatures require profile changes that reduce repeatability and increase production waste.
cases.quote: Roasters sample roast and creat a profile on a small roaster (usually 1kg drum size) with a batch size of 200-1000g.
cases.label: TOPICAL
cases.reason: Neutral explanation of how sample roasting works.

cases.pain_title: Cannot scale sample roast settings to café production volume
cases.pain_description: Café-based and wholesale roasters struggle to scale sample roast settings to larger production batches. Different batch sizes and drop temperatures require profile changes that reduce repeatability and increase production waste.
cases.quote: This profile is then “copied” and used on a larger batch with the goal being the same results as the sample roast.
cases.label: TOPICAL
cases.reason: Neutral process description, no expressed failure.

cases.pain_title: Cannot predict café brew performance from traditional cupping

cases.quote: In my experience (as a barista for 7 years and a working at a roaster for another 3), traditional cupping is primarily geared towards green coffee purchasing.
cases.label: TOPICAL
cases.reason: States cupping's purpose, doesn't assert prediction failure.

cases.pain_title: Cannot connect green coffee purchasing decisions to customer brew outcomes

cases.pain_title: Cannot schedule roast to order for retail and wholesale freshness windows
cases.pain_description: Roasteries cannot use one policy for retail coffee that should ship within 24h of roast and wholesale espresso that needs degassing for 5-7 days. Café schedules, retail backstock, and subscription shipping require different production timing.
cases.quote: It seems to be a dying business model to advertise roast to order anyway since it has become more and more well-known that resting most coffees for at least a few days, and in many cases, a week or two, makes them taste better.
cases.label: TOPICAL

cases.pain_title: Cannot submit complete setlists to PROs after shows
cases.pain_description: Venues and performers lack a consistent workflow for collecting setlists and reporting live performances to ASCAP, BMI, and SESAC. Responsibility for submitting performance information remains unclear.
cases.quote: How PROs track live performances Venues above a certain size report setlists to PROs either directly or via services like [Setlist.fm](http://Setlist.fm) (which PROs increasingly use as a data source).
cases.label: TOPICAL
cases.reason: Neutral explanatory description of how PRO tracking works, not an expressed submission failure.
